channel.title: The Local France - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Local France (thelocal.fr)

item.title: French teachers call nationwide strike over budget cuts
item.description: Five of France's largest teaching unions have called a nationwide strike in protest at what they describe as 'austerity' budget plans for education.

item.title: Which countries in Europe have the biggest share of foreign residents?
item.description: In 2025, people born outside the European Union made up about 10 percent of the EU’s 450 million population. But which countries have the largest share of foreign-born residents?

item.title: 'It seems very unfair': Key questions answered on French citizenship changes
item.description: France's rules on citizenship have undergone several big changes in the last year - so we held a live Q&amp;A to answer the key questions from members of The Local. Here's a roundup of the main topics.

item.title: French government expands obligatory wildfire prevention work for homeowners
item.description: Laws require many homeowners in the south of France to do compulsory works each year to help prevent the spread of wildfires - but as fires become more common, the laws have been expanded to cover properties in northern France, including Brittany.

item.title: New Nice mayor poses a 'real problem' for 2030 Winter Olympics
item.description: The 2030 Winter Olympics in the French Alps, already bedevilled by several senior executives quitting, faces another potential headache with the election of far-right politician Eric Ciotti as mayor of Nice.

item.title: 600-year-old pinot noir grape found in medieval French toilet
item.description: A 600-year-old grape seed discovered in the toilets of a medieval French hospital is genetically identical to the grapes still being used to make pinot noir wine, scientists said on Tuesday.

item.title: France relaxes criteria for blood donors - but Brits are still banned
item.description: The French health authority has announced the relaxation of certain criteria around who can donate blood, but those who spent time in the UK during the BSE crisis are still banned.

item.title: REVEALED: French chefs' favourite wines priced between €11 and €50
item.description: Six of France's Michelin-starred chefs have revealed their top choices for the wines they drink themselves, all priced under €50. Here's what they recommend.

item.title: French films with English subtitles to watch in April 2026
item.description: A Romy Schneider must-see, a belated Easter celebration, a biopic set in occupied France, and a Jean-Luc Godard classic all feature on Lost in Frenchlation’s April listings of French films with English subtitles.

item.title: OPINION: For foreigners in France, each election brings a creeping sense of dread
item.description: The Local France's editor Emma Pearson explains why foreigners in France face an anxious year ahead as the presidential election looms large and the threat from the xenophobic far right grows ever stronger.

item.title: Paris: Hundreds evacuated as fire rips through 5-star Le Bristol hotel
item.description: Hundreds of people were evacuated on Wednesday morning as a fire ripped through one of the French capital's most famous hotels, situated close to the president's Elysée Palace.

item.title: France's Lille to host new EU customs authority
item.description: The northern French city of Lille will host the future European Union customs authority, officials said on Wednesday, as the bloc seeks to stem the flow of cheap Chinese parcel imports.

item.title: Americans in Paris to host 'biggest ever' No Kings protest
item.description: Americans in France are planning another No Kings protest against the US regime of Donald Trump, which they expect to attract several thousand people, both American and French.

item.title: France jails ex-policeman for raping domestic abuse victim
item.description: A French court on Wednesday jailed a former police officer for 12 years for raping a woman who came to report domestic abuse.

item.title: When do the clocks change in France this year?
item.description: The clocks went forward an hour in early March in most of USA and Canada — but Europeans think that’s a bit premature.
